short_description: Consumer-facing lifestyle trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal for chronotype tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing lifestyle trait with practical raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited morningness-eveningness tendency and real-world sleep schedule for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with chronotype tendency, meaning a relative inclination toward earlier or later sleep-wake preference, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Chronotype tendency is presented here as a cautious relative lifestyle signal, not as a direct schedule prescription or a diagnosis of any sleep condition. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic real-world result or as a direct readout of your current sleep schedule.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.

Real-world chronotype expression also depends strongly on age, work and school schedule, artificial light exposure, parenting, sleep debt, and behavior, so this should not be treated as a deterministic prediction of actual daily routine.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
